_what: Villa Nilly concierge context. Tier 1 is the guide; tier 2 is the appliances; tier 3 is the island reference library. English source; the model answers in the page's language.

villa.name: Villa Nilly
villa.where: Parc de la Baie Orientale, Orient Bay, Saint-Martin (French side)
villa.note: The villa’s own site is on its way.

dining.name: Ratafia
dining.hook: Premium cocktails and a sunset terrace at Porto Cupecoy.
dining.desc: A cocktail lounge at Porto Cupecoy where owner and mixologist Max makes the drinks, backed by a serious wine and champagne list, cigars, and caviar. The ocean-facing terrace is the spot for sunset. Cash only — reach them by email or Instagram, there's no phone line. Open Monday–Friday from 5:30pm, Saturday from 9:30pm, closed Sunday.
dining.address: 1 Niger Road, Top Floor, Cupecoy Bay
dining.meals_note: drinks in the evening — no dinner

dining.name: 3 Amigos
dining.hook: The island's Tex-Mex spot, on Maho's casino strip.
dining.desc: The only real Tex-Mex on the island, upstairs across from Casino Royale in Maho. Lobster enchiladas, skirt steak fajitas, tableside guacamole, and TVs for the game. Taco Tuesday runs $2 tacos all day. We've only been for lunch, so we can't speak for it after dark.
dining.address: 1 Rhine Road, Maho, Sint Maarten
dining.meals_note: lunch is what we vouch for; may open limited nights — check before going

dining.name: Grumpy’s
dining.hook: Laid-back sports and music bar by the Philipsburg marina.
dining.desc: A locals' bar at Dock Maarten, between the cruise port and the center of Philipsburg — cold drinks, a game on the screen, music, and none of the cruise-ship crush. An easy stop when you're in town.
dining.address: 26 Juancho Yrausquin Blvd, Dock Maarten

dining.name: Sexy Beef
dining.hook: Legendary roadside lolo — Caribbean BBQ, no ceremony.
dining.desc: A roadside lolo that everyone on the island knows. The name is the owner's nickname, courtesy of her boyfriend. The thing to order is the satay — beef, chicken and pork skewers under a peanut sauce you'll want extra of for the fries and tostones. One of the few lolos with a full bar, and the margaritas have a reputation. Lively on weekends when the locals come out.
dining.address: Front Street 28, Philipsburg, Sint Maarten

dining.name: Babacool
dining.hook: The only beach club on the island with a pool.
dining.desc: The only beach club on the island with a pool, on Simpson Bay Beach between Karakter and Mary's Boon — all white and pink, and quickly one of the busiest spots on the Dutch side. The kitchen is run by Jérôme Ferrer, a Michelin-starred chef, so the food is a level above the usual beach lunch: ceviche, good cocktails, and DJs from the afternoon through sunset. You can arrive by car, by boat or by jet ski.
dining.address: 121 Simpson Bay Rd

dining.name: Bamboo House
dining.hook: Sushi and steak in a restored hilltop plantation house.
dining.desc: Sushi and steak in a restored 19th-century sugar mill on Diamond Hill, with Simpson Bay and the sunset laid out below — a fixture for over twenty years. Most Thursday evenings the band Sugar Apple plays, and that is one of our favorite nights out on the island.
dining.address: 150 Union Road, Cole Bay, Sint Maarten

dining.name: Dinghy Dock
dining.hook: Craft beer and cheerful chaos, beloved by sailors.
dining.desc: A sailors' bar in Simpson Bay with the island's best beer list — over a hundred bottles and rotating drafts — and a cheerful, slightly chaotic way of doing things: the bottles come to the table and you mix your own. Order the fish dip and the stuffed shrimp poppers. No reservations, a game on every screen, families by day and a louder crowd late.
dining.address: #46 Airport Road, Simpson Bay, Sint Maarten

dining.name: Zee Best Bakeshop
dining.hook: French bakery near the airport, going since 1983.
dining.desc: The take-out counter of Zee Best, the Dutch side's French bakery since 1983, on Airport Road a minute from the terminal. Almond croissants, pains au chocolat, cinnamon rolls and scones baked each morning, plus sandwiches, quiches, salads and smoothies. A good stop on the way to a flight.
dining.address: #100 Airport Road, Simpson Bay, Sint Maarten

dining.name: Calmos Café
dining.hook: Back on Grand Case beach after six years closed by Irma.
dining.desc: Reopened in 2023 after Irma kept it shut for six years, and back on Grand Case beach where it belongs. French cooking with a Caribbean heart — duck confit, shrimp and scallop ravioli, lobster ravioli, and a mahi tartare people come back for. Good cocktails, no dress code. Daily, 4:30pm to midnight.
dining.address: 40 Boulevard de Grand Case

dining.name: Captain Frenchy by Fred
dining.hook: Gallic beach bar on the Grand Case sand.
dining.desc: A Grand Case beach bar that has been there for years and is French through and through. By day it's lounge chairs with waiter service — tapas, burgers, a salade niçoise with your feet in the sand. In the evening the kitchen goes fully French: scallops in beurre blanc, frog legs, beef tartare, with the lights of Anguilla across the water. Live music, DJs and the occasional beach party Thursday through Saturday.
dining.address: 184 Boulevard de Grand Case, Grand Case, 97150 St. Martin

dining.name: Java
dining.hook: Mediterranean plates and cocktails, right on the beach.
dining.desc: Mediterranean cooking on the Grand Case strip, with a wooden deck out over the water. Plates to share and a few full entrées — lobster, truffle pasta, slow-cooked lamb shoulder, a beef tenderloin flambéed at the table. Come at sunset for the cocktails; some evenings there's live music.
dining.address: 70 Boulevard de Grand Case, Grand Case, 97150 St. Martin

dining.name: Le Carpaccio
dining.hook: Real Italian, tucked just off the restaurant row.
dining.desc: A small Italian spot tucked inside the Parc Phenix commercial center just off Grand Case's restaurant row. Homemade pastas, wood-fired pizzas with prosciutto and buffalo mozzarella, and seafood like linguine ai frutti di mare and grilled branzino. Good Italian wine list, classic desserts — tiramisu, panna cotta, cannoli. Lunch only, Monday through Saturday.
dining.address: Coral Palm N°11, Parc Phenix, Route de l’Espérance, Grand Case, 97150 St. Martin

dining.name: L’Auberge Gourmande
dining.hook: Classic fine French in a 19th-century Creole house.
dining.desc: Fine French cooking in a 120-year-old Creole house on the Grand Case boulevard, since 1979. Alexandre cooks and Chantal runs the room — escargots, frog legs, onion soup, a veal chop, the baked salmon they're known for — and the long wine list comes with a sommelier to steer you. A Caribbean Travel & Life "Best of Caribbean" winner.
dining.address: 89 Boulevard de Grand Case, Grand Case, 97150 St. Martin

dining.name: La Quintessence
dining.hook: Artisan pizza and fresh pasta, unfussy and good.
dining.desc: From the team behind the St. Barts original, La Quintessence brings artisan sourdough pizza to Grand Case — an 18-hour sourdough crust with organic Italian flour, thin, crispy, and light. Beyond the pizzas (try the truffle or burrata), there's fresh pasta served in crispy pizza-dough bowls, salads, and calzones. A cozy patio and a rooftop terrace with ocean views.
dining.address: 101 Boulevard de Grand Case, Grand Case, 97150 St. Martin

dining.name: Le Pressoir
dining.hook: Grand Case's gastronomic landmark, in an old salt press.
dining.desc: Grand Case's top table for fine dining, set in a century-old Creole house. Chef Jerome Droingt has been named Caribbean Restaurant of the Year and ranked among the region's top 50 for several years running. Signature dishes: five-hour braised octopus, smoked wahoo, Rossini tenderloin with truffle. A deep wine list (250+ selections) and 150+ Caribbean rums at the attached bar, La Part des Anges. Dinner only, Monday–Saturday, 5–11pm.
dining.address: 30 Boulevard de Grand Case, Grand Case, 97150 St. Martin

dining.name: MÖKA Café SXM
dining.hook: Brunch, smoothies and good coffee to start the day.
dining.desc: On the Grand Case boulevard in the old Mood space — whitewashed arches, warm wood, a neighborhood-café feel. Brunch and smoothies by day, and a good morning stop before you walk the restaurant row. Open until 5pm, kitchen until 4pm.
dining.address: 48 Boulevard de Grand Case, Grand-Case, 97150 St. Martin

dining.name: Quai 58
dining.hook: Grand Case's sunset watering hole, at the top of the dinghy dock.
dining.desc: Quai 58 sits at the top of the dinghy dock in Grand Case, the happening watering hole in town. Owner Gaby keeps it easy and social — tapas, drinks, and a front-row sunset, with weekend DJs adding energy after dark. It's about the scene more than the menu.
dining.address: 58 Boulevard de Grand Case

dining.name: Coco Beach
dining.hook: Beach club minutes from the villa — loungers and long lunches.
dining.desc: A chic beach club on Orient Bay — wood and white, sea in front — with refined French cooking and Mediterranean and Caribbean touches: lunch from a gazebo or a lounge chair, cocktails at sunset.
dining.address: Parc de la Baie Orientale, Orient Bay Beach, 97150 Saint-Martin

dining.name: Kontiki Beach Restaurant
dining.hook: French-Asian cooking with your feet in the sand.
dining.desc: The first restaurant built on Orient Beach, in 1989, and still the one under the red umbrellas. French cooking with an Asian side — crispy red tuna, sushi rolls, a roast farm chicken carved at the table, duck foie gras. On weekends a DJ plays through the afternoon until sunset, so pick your day by the mood you want.
dining.address: Baie Orientale, Orient Bay Beach, 97150 Saint-Martin

dining.name: L’Atelier
dining.hook: Steak and seafood on the bay, Gault Millau recognized.
dining.desc: L'Atelier is Orient Bay's steakhouse specialist, with owner Alexandre walking you through a chalkboard menu that changes nightly. Expect serious meat — Japanese Wagyu, USDA Prime Black Angus, Portuguese Minhota Gallega, Iberico black pig — cooked simply and well.
dining.address: Place du Village, Baie Orientale, 97150 Saint-Martin

dining.name: Le P’tit Bistro
dining.hook: The neighborhood French bistro, done right.
dining.desc: Jerome and Manon have run this little French bistro for over fifteen years, and it shows — generous, traditional cooking, specials that change weekly, and a real welcome. Seafood platters come in fresh each week.
dining.address: Village Place, Orient Bay

dining.name: Les Galets
dining.hook: A gastronomic table d'hôtes, a short stroll away.
dining.desc: A table d'hôtes in the garden of a small hotel near Orient Bay: one five-course menu, new each week, French and seasonal, served by the pool with the tree frogs going. Every evening except Wednesday; reserve on WhatsApp — it's essential.
dining.address: Lot 45, Les Jardins d’Orient Bay, 97150 St. Martin

dining.name: Maison Mère
dining.hook: French cooking with a Creole accent, close to home.
dining.desc: The name means "Mom's House," and Maison Mère lives up to it — refined French home cooking with Caribbean warmth, everything made in-house from starter to dessert. The intimate Orient Bay Village setting and a strong cocktail list make it an easy pick for a real dinner close to home.
dining.address: Place de la Baie Orientale, Orient Bay, 97150 Saint-Martin

dining.name: Orange Fever
dining.hook: Orient Bay beach bar — lounge chairs, rum, no rush.
dining.desc: A casual, easygoing beach spot on Orient Bay — French and Caribbean dishes, good cocktails, and artisanal pizzas people keep coming back for. Grab a beach chair and umbrella and have lunch brought right to you on the sand.
dining.address: Rue de la Baie Orientale, Orient Bay Beach, 97150 Saint-Martin

dining.name: The Perch Bar & Grill
dining.hook: Grill and cocktails at the clothing-optional end of Orient Bay.
dining.desc: The only beach bar on the clothing-optional southern end of Orient Beach, on the site of the former Club Orient resort. The Perch serves grilled-to-order barbecue ribs, fresh mahi, garlic shrimp, cheeseburgers, and frozen cocktails at prices well below the beach clubs up north. Cash only (USD and euros accepted at 1:1).
dining.address: Club Orient, Orient Beach, 97150 St. Martin

dining.name: Roasty’s
dining.hook: Café and rotisserie — coffee in, roast chicken out.
dining.desc: A café and rotisserie near Orient Bay Village. The chicken is the point — crisp skin, juicy inside, sitting in its own drippings — and around it lobster rolls, focaccia pizzas and paninis. Regulars swear the tiramisu is the best on the island. Easy for lunch — and check with them about dinner nights.
dining.address: 261 Avenue Des Plages, Orient Bay, 97150 Saint-Martin
dining.meals_note: lunch is what we know; may do limited dinner nights — check before going

dining.name: SAO Asian Factory
dining.hook: Pan-Asian across four kitchens, minutes from the villa.
dining.desc: Elodie and Loick's pan-Asian place in Orient Bay Village, a two-minute walk from the villa. Order the mahi-mahi tartare and the wakame salmon — both house specialties.
dining.address: Place du Village, Baie Orientale, 97150 Saint-Martin

dining.name: BZH
dining.hook: One of our favorite dinners out on the island — Breton cooking done right.
dining.desc: Brittany in the Caribbean: Aurélien cooks and Laetitia runs the place — real buckwheat galettes and sweet crêpes beside a short menu of French classics that changes every two weeks, all made in-house. French wines and Breton ciders. Several palm-shaded terraces for dinner under the stars, live music now and then. Monday to Saturday, evenings.
dining.address: 72 Rue de Coralita, Oyster Pond, 97150 St. Martin

dining.name: Le Cool’Heure
dining.hook: Home-style Creole and French cooking, off in La Savane.
dining.desc: Chef Betty runs the kitchen at this small bistro out in La Savane, just outside Grand Case on the way to Marigot, turning out daily specials, butcher's cuts and whatever looked good at the market that morning. It's home-style Creole and French cooking, no pretense — the kind of place with regulars rather than a view. Save room for the dessert of the day, made in-house. Lunch only, Monday to Saturday, cash only.
dining.address: 123 Route de la Savane, La Savane, 97150 Saint-Martin

dining.name: Be Kool
dining.hook: Family-run French bistro, right on the Marigot waterfront.
dining.desc: A family affair — Dad previously of Tropicana, with two of his sons now in the kitchen — serving confident French cooking right on the Marigot waterfront, close enough to Marina Port la Royale to tie up a dinghy in front of the sidewalk seating. Expect foie gras, duck, lamb and escargots, plus a wine list that's taken seriously. It occupies the old Chanteclair spot. We've only ever had lunch here, but it's a place people consistently love.
dining.address: Marina Port la Royale, 97150 Marigot, Saint-Martin

dining.name: Ô Plongeoir
dining.hook: Twenty-plus years on the Marigot waterfront, feet from the bay.
dining.desc: A fixture of the Marigot waterfront for more than twenty years, sitting right outside the marina, Ô Plongeoir serves French and Creole cooking with the bay right below the terrace. Go for the teriyaki tuna tataki, the pastis-flambéed shrimp, or a real seafood pasta, and stay for the house digestif — 'ti bitin' — they send out at the end of the meal. Open non-stop from 9am for coffee and pastries straight through lunch. Credit cards accepted.
dining.address: 13 Boulevard du Docteur Hubert Petit, 97150 Marigot, Saint-Martin

dining.name: Le Marocain
dining.hook: Moroccan classics and mint tea, tucked into Marigot.
dining.desc: Real Moroccan cooking on the French side — tagines, couscous, mint tea — in a small, atmospheric room in Marigot. It's dinner only, six nights a week, and it fills up — call ahead to reserve. Friday nights sometimes bring a live belly dancer — worth calling ahead if you want to catch the show. It's a genuine change of pace from the island's usual French and Creole menus. Cash accepted.
dining.address: 169 Rue de Hollande, 97150 Marigot, Saint-Martin

dining.name: Le Temps des Cerises
dining.hook: Our favorite beach club in Grand Case — Creole and seafood from breakfast on.
dining.desc: The restaurant at LTC La Plage, right on Grand Case beach, built around Creole cooking and whatever the boats brought in — fish nems, octopus salad, seafood platters piled high. It runs non-stop from breakfast at 8am through lunch and dinner, seven days a week, so it's an easy one to fold into a beach day. Tables spill toward the sand, and the setting does a lot of the work.
dining.address: 158 Boulevard de Grand Case, Grand Case, 97150 Saint-Martin

dining.name: Bistrot Caraïbes
dining.hook: French fine dining on Grand Case's restaurant row.
dining.desc: One of Grand Case's steadier names, on the boulevard among the restaurant row, doing French classics without fuss — foie gras, lobster thermidor, duck breast, a full cheese course. The dining room is small and air-conditioned, so it's a good pick when the evening's too warm for an open terrace. Ask for JC if he's on — an island character everyone knows, nights here and days at Orange Fever. Reservations recommended.
dining.address: 81 Boulevard de Grand Case, 97150 Saint-Martin

dining.name: Momohana
dining.hook: Asian fusion in Cole Bay, plated like art.
dining.desc: A newer name in Cole Bay, plating Asian fusion built on European technique — the kitchen calls it a daily 'opus' from whatever's freshest that morning. The room and presentation lean upscale for the neighborhood. Open for lunch Monday to Saturday, noon to 3pm, and dinner Monday to Saturday, 6 to 9:30pm.
dining.address: ARK Building, Diamond Estate, Red Plum Tree, 7 Union Road, Cole Bay, Sint Maarten
dining.meals_note: lunch only as far as we know (the record’s 12–3 hours agree); may do limited dinner nights — check before going

dining.name: Sint Maarten Yacht Club Bar & Restaurant
dining.hook: Front-row seats for the mega-yachts, at the Simpson Bay bridge.
dining.desc: Right at the Simpson Bay bridge, with the lower deck putting you as close to the passing mega-yachts as you'll get without a slip of your own. It's open all day, 7am to midnight, from breakfast and their well-known eggs Benedict through happy hour and dinner. Ask staff for the day's rough bridge-opening times if you want to catch the boats moving. Casual, easy, and popular with the sailing crowd.
dining.address: 90 Welfare Road, Simpson Bay, Sint Maarten

dining.name: Anse Marcel Beach
dining.hook: Beach club at the quiet end of the island, in Anse Marcel.
dining.desc: The beach restaurant at Le Domaine Anse Marcel, serving French and Caribbean cooking with breakfast and lunch service looking straight out over the bay. It's part of a bigger resort that also runs the more formal Le Gourmet in the evenings. Reviews are mixed on service and price, so it's worth going in with the right expectations. Good for a change-of-scenery lunch on the quieter, French end of the island.
dining.address: 26 Rue de Lonvilliers, Anse Marcel, 97150 Saint-Martin

dining.name: Ti Palm
dining.hook: Caribbean dining at Hôtel Palm Court, near Orient Bay.
dining.desc: Traditional Caribbean cooking at Hôtel Palm Court, near Orient Bay — brunch on weekends, and a real sit-down dinner Tuesday through Saturday, with a warm, easygoing welcome.
dining.address: Hôtel Palm Court, Orient Bay, 97150 Saint-Martin

dining.name: La Trattoria
dining.hook: Handmade Italian pasta and pizza, red-brick trattoria charm in Orient Bay.
dining.desc: A cozy, classic trattoria — red decor, brick walls, checkered tablecloths — serving handmade pasta, focaccia pizzas, linguine with truffle, and veal Milanese. Vegan and gluten-free options available, plus a daily fish special. Opens nightly from 5pm.
dining.address: Rue de la Baie Orientale, 97150 Saint-Martin

dining.name: La Favela
dining.hook: Jungle-style cocktail bar and Caribbean-Latin fusion in Orient Bay village.
dining.desc: Jungle décor in Orient Bay village — wooden tables, sofas, a pool table, low light — and Caribbean-Latin cooking: cod fritters, tacos, quesadillas, chicken colombo, grilled meats, ceviche, and lobster straight from the tank.
dining.address: La Place du Village, Orient Bay, 97150 Saint-Martin

dining.name: Yellow Sub
dining.hook: All-day beachfront brasserie in Orient Bay — breakfast through late night.
dining.desc: On the beach in Orient Bay and open all day — a real breakfast, an easy lunch, then live music Thursday through Saturday and sports on the screens at night. Right on the sand, no airs. Daily, 7:30am to 2am.
dining.address: Résidence de la Plage, Parc de la Baie Orientale, 97150 Saint-Martin

dining.name: Good Morning
dining.hook: Bagels, pastries and a shaded terrace to start the day in Orient Bay.
dining.desc: Good Morning is the neighborhood spot for New York-style bagels, flaky croissants and a strong coffee, with a shaded terrace just back from the beach. It's an easy stop before or after Orient Bay — quiches, paninis and salads carry it through if breakfast turns into lunch. Order at the counter and grab a table on the terrace; it fills up fast on cruise-ship mornings. Open daily, roughly 7am to early afternoon.
dining.address: 13 Orient Bay Plaza, Baie Orientale, 97150 Saint-Martin

dining.name: Bona Mama
dining.hook: Award-winning pizza and rotisserie, voted Best Table of Saint Martin.
dining.desc: Bona Mama is a low-key pizzeria-rotisserie tucked into the Orient Bay Plaza, doing wood-fired pizza, spit-roasted meats, charcuterie boards and a fairly priced wine list — and it took home the 'Best Table of Saint Martin' award at the 2025/26 Gastronomy Festival, judged blind by a panel of chefs. Good for a casual dinner out or a pizza to take back to the villa. Open evenings on weekdays, all day on weekends; delivery around Orient Bay is available.
dining.address: Lot 42, Plaza Orient Bay, Baie Orientale, 97150 Saint-Martin

beaches.name: Orient Bay
beaches.hook: Two kilometers of sand at the bottom of the hill, and the beach clubs along it.
beaches.desc:
The long east-facing crescent the villa looks down on, and the busiest beach on the French side. The middle is a run of beach clubs — lounge chairs, lunch, a shower and a parking spot for the day — with Kontiki, Coco Beach and Bikini Beach among them. The trade wind blows onshore most of the year, so there is usually small chop and always somebody on a kayak or a paddleboard. The northern end toward the Green Cay side is quieter and free of loungers. Morning is calmest; the wind builds through the afternoon.

The far southern end, beyond the last of the clubs at the old Club Orient site, is the island's only official clothing-optional beach — everyone calls it Club O. The Perch Bar & Grill sits in the middle of that stretch. It is a distinct section with clothed beach either side of it, not something you wander into by accident.

beaches.name: Îlet Pinel
beaches.hook: Five minutes on a ferry: clear shallow water, two restaurants, nothing else.
beaches.desc:
A small nature-reserve island off Cul-de-Sac, and the day trip most of our guests end up doing twice. The crossing takes about five minutes. The west-facing beach is sheltered and shallow, with Karibuni and Yellow Beach set back in the trees for lunch and loungers.

A path starts behind the left-hand restaurant and crosses the island — up, then down, five to ten minutes. The north-facing beach on the other side is quieter, rockier, has the better snorkeling, and is where people swim without swimwear. Unofficially, like everywhere except Club O.

beaches.name: Tintamarre
beaches.hook: An empty island with a mud bath and turtles in the bay. Boat only.
beaches.desc: Uninhabited, part of the nature reserve, reachable only by boat. The bay has a long pale beach, green turtles that graze close in, and the gray clay bank people coat themselves in before rinsing off. No facilities of any kind.

beaches.name: Anse Marcel
beaches.hook: A deep, quiet bay on the north coast where the sea barely moves.
beaches.desc: Tucked behind a headland and a marina, which makes it one of the most sheltered beaches on the island — flat water on days when Orient Bay is white. The resort takes up most of the sand and runs the loungers and the beach restaurant, but the beach itself is public like every beach in France. The road in is a long climb over the hill from Grand Case.

beaches.name: Happy Bay
beaches.hook: Ten minutes on foot over the headland, and most days it is yours alone.
beaches.desc:
There is no road to Happy Bay. You park at Friar's Bay, take the path up the left-hand headland and drop down the other side — about ten minutes, in shoes rather than flip-flops. What you get is a curve of pale sand with palms behind it, no buildings, no loungers and usually no one. Sunset here is one of the best on the island, but don't leave the walk back until it's fully dark.

Clothing is optional here by custom rather than by rule — most obviously midweek, and at the quiet ends near the rocks. On weekends, when people come over from Friar's Bay, it's topless at most.

beaches.name: Friar's Bay
beaches.hook: A sheltered cove with two beach bars and water calm enough to forget about.
beaches.desc: A short, protected bay on the north-west coast, a world away from Orient Bay's wind. Two beach bars sit on the sand — good for a long lunch and a rum — and the swimming is gentle enough for children. It fills up on weekends with people from Marigot, which is part of its charm. Also the starting point for the walk over to Happy Bay.

beaches.name: Grand Case Beach
beaches.hook: Swim in front of the restaurant village, then stay for dinner and the sunset.
beaches.desc: The strip of sand directly behind Grand Case's single street. The water is calm and the bottom is sandy, and several of the restaurants open straight onto the beach, so an afternoon swim can turn into dinner without moving the car. The sun goes down behind Anguilla from here, which is the whole point of arriving by six.

beaches.name: Baie Rouge
beaches.hook: Long, open and faintly pink, with a rock arch at the far end worth the walk.
beaches.desc: One of the best-looking beaches on the island — a wide sweep of pinkish sand on the Terres Basses, facing open sea. Walk west along the sand and you reach the eroded rock arches and the little cove behind them. Because it faces the swell there is often a shore break, so it is not the one for nervous swimmers. A beach bar sits at the eastern end for chairs and a drink.

beaches.name: Baie aux Prunes
beaches.hook: Quiet all summer, and where the island surfs when the winter swell arrives.
beaches.desc: A small west-facing bay on the Terres Basses with nothing built on it. In summer it is flat, clear and almost empty. From roughly December the north swell wraps in and the local surfers appear. Good snorkeling along the rocks at either end when the sea is down.

beaches.name: Baie Longue
beaches.hook: The island's longest beach, with nothing on it — and its best sunset.
beaches.desc: The longest beach on St. Martin and the emptiest for its size. No beach bars, no loungers, no shade — just sand, sea and the hotel at the far eastern end. The bottom shelves quickly in places and there can be an undertow, so swim where you can see the bottom.

beaches.name: Great Bay
beaches.hook: Philipsburg's own beach, with the boardwalk and the whole town behind it.
beaches.desc: A long calm curve of sand right in front of Philipsburg, with the boardwalk — bars, restaurants, shops — running its whole length. It is also where the cruise passengers land, so on a two-ship day it is packed and on a no-ship day it is oddly quiet. Check the cruise schedule before committing to it.

beaches.name: Simpson Bay Beach
beaches.hook: A long flat strip with the bars behind it and aircraft passing low overhead.
beaches.desc: Two kilometers of straight sand along the Dutch side's restaurant and bar strip, so you can swim, eat and drink without moving. The western end sits under the approach to Princess Juliana — not the jet blast of Maho, just aircraft passing low overhead, which is pleasant rather than alarming.

beaches.name: Maho Beach
beaches.hook: Aircraft land over your head. Stand well back when they take off.
beaches.desc: The small beach at the end of the Princess Juliana runway, and the island's most photographed thing. Arriving aircraft clear the road by a few meters. Take the departure warnings seriously: the jet blast from a large aircraft will knock an adult over and has hurt people here.

beaches.name: Mullet Bay
beaches.hook: Golden sand, waves to body-surf, lounge chairs and food trucks. The Dutch side's best.
beaches.desc: Consistently rated the best beach on the Dutch side: a deep curve of golden sand backed by sea grape, with the old golf course behind. Waves are big enough to body-surf without being a problem — a favorite with anyone in their teens.

beaches.name: Cupecoy Beach
beaches.hook: Small coves under carved sandstone cliffs, and the west end's famous sunset.
beaches.desc:
Not one beach but a series of small coves under soft sandstone cliffs the sea has undercut into overhangs and caves. How much sand there is depends on the season and the last swell. Waves and a shore break are normal here.

It is also the Dutch side's clothing-optional beach — unofficially, the way Happy Bay is. Which cove is busy changes with the day, and the coves are separate enough that you can pick one to suit.

activities.name: Bacchus
activities.hook: Serious wine cellar and deli, with a very good lunch hidden behind it.
activities.desc: A wine cellar, delicatessen and bistronomic restaurant in one, tucked behind the Super U at Hope Estate — French and international wines, champagnes, rums, fine foods and cigars. Lunch only, until 3pm. Hard to find the first time; worth it.
activities.address: 18 Rue Anegada, Hope Estate, 97150 Saint-Martin

activities.name: Balaou
activities.hook: A bar that floats off Grand Case — free dinghy out from the Quai 58 dock.
activities.desc: French Saint Martin's only floating bar, dreamed up by Johan Pidoux — the same Captain Jo — with friends Kevin and Nicolas. Floating loungers with your feet in the water, lounge chairs, inflatables at no extra charge. Flyboard lessons Thursday to Sunday with Aquasports SXM, live DJs Friday and Sunday afternoons. Open daily 11am until sunset. Message them and they will send a dinghy from the wooden dock at Quai 58.
activities.address: Off Grand Case bay — dinghy from the Quai 58 dock

activities.name: Bikini Watersports
activities.hook: Jet skis, paddleboards, kayaks and parasailing, right on Orient Beach.
activities.desc: Twenty years on Orient Beach, next to Bikini Beach restaurant. Jet ski (minimum age sixteen to drive, younger as a passenger), flyboard, banana boat, tubing, kayaks, paddleboards, snorkel gear and parasailing. Open daily from 9am.
activities.address: Orient Beach, Baie Orientale, 97150 Saint-Martin

activities.name: Boutique COSY SXM
activities.hook: Furniture and decoration, indoor and out, at the Cul de Sac roundabout.
activities.desc: A décor and furniture boutique at the Cul de Sac roundabout by Hope Estate. Monday to Saturday, 9:30am–12:30pm and 2pm–6pm.
activities.address: Rond-point de Cul de Sac, Place Péninsule, Hope Estate, 97150 Saint-Martin

activities.name: Captain Jo Boat Charter
activities.hook: Four boats out of Anse Marcel, with a captain, for a day wherever you like.
activities.desc: A small skippered charter operation out of Anse Marcel with a fleet of four — a Powercat 40, two Boston Whalers and a Kiwi 27. Day trips, island-hopping and custom itineraries.
activities.address: Anse Marcel, 97150 Saint-Martin

activities.name: Colibri Massage
activities.hook: Massage in a cabana by the sea at Coco Beach, five minutes away.
activities.desc: Tania and her team work from Coco Beach and KKO on Orient Bay, blending Californian, Thai, Reiki and intuitive technique. There is a private cabana by the water for couples. Bookable online.
activities.address: Coco Beach, Baie Orientale, 97150 Saint-Martin

activities.name: Del Mar Boutique
activities.hook: Handpicked European pieces cut for the heat.
activities.desc: A small fashion boutique on Billy Folly Road carrying European labels chosen for the climate — light fabrics, easy shapes, for men and women.
activities.address: Billy Folly Road, Simpson Bay, Sint Maarten

activities.name: Devil’s Cupper
activities.hook: A flat coastal walk to natural tide pools where the Atlantic hits the rocks.
activities.desc: A short, mostly flat trail along Guana Bay to the tide pools known as Devil's Cupper. The footing is tricky in places and the Atlantic side can be rough — worth shoes with grip. Access is at the end of Pelican Road.
activities.address: End of Pelican Road, Point Blanche, Sint Maarten

activities.name: En Vogue
activities.hook: Michaela's boutique — linen, boho-chic and small designers you won't find elsewhere.
activities.desc: Fifteen years and more of Michaela's eye: boho-chic, casual chic, linen dresses, handmade jewelry and bags from small designers around the world. Monday to Saturday, 9am–6pm.
activities.address: Billy Folly Rd #3B

activities.name: Ferry to Anguilla
activities.hook: Twenty minutes from Marigot to one of the best stretches of sand anywhere.
activities.desc: The public ferry leaves Marigot roughly hourly from 8:30am to 6pm, returning from Blowing Point 7:30am to 5:15pm. About twenty minutes each way. Around $30 one way, cash on board, plus a small passenger fee at the ticket office. Anguilla charges its own departure tax on the way back. Bring a passport.
activities.address: Marigot Ferry Terminal, 97150 Saint-Martin

activities.name: Ferry to St. Barts
activities.hook: Under an hour to Gustavia — go for the day, come back for dinner.
activities.desc: Two operators run the crossing: Voyager from Marigot, about an hour, and Great Bay Express from Bobby's Marina in Philipsburg, about forty-five minutes. Roughly €70–110 one way. Reserve ahead in season, take a passport — and something for the swell if you're prone to it.
activities.address: Marigot Ferry Terminal or Bobby's Marina, Philipsburg

activities.name: Le Goût du Vin
activities.hook: Marigot's long-standing wine cellar — French and international, by the bottle.
activities.desc: An importer and retailer in Marigot, over thirty years in the business, with a couple of thousand references in French and international wines, champagnes and spirits. The place to go for something specific rather than something cold.
activities.address: 37 Boulevard de France (Front de Mer), 97150 Marigot

activities.name: Loterie Farm
activities.hook: Jungle pool, ziplines and lunch under the trees at the foot of Pic Paradis.
activities.desc: A private nature reserve on the slopes below Pic Paradis: spring-water pool, ziplines, hiking trails and the Jungle Room restaurant among the trees. Zipline departures run at 10am, noon and 2pm daily — sign up at reception at least fifteen minutes before.
activities.address: Rue du Pic Paradis, 97150 Saint-Martin

activities.name: Minguet Art Gallery
activities.hook: Alexandre Minguet's landscapes, on the hill between Marigot and Grand Case.
activities.desc: The Minguet family gallery on Rambaud hill, showing the late Alexandre Minguet's Caribbean landscapes alongside other island artists. Originals and prints. Monday to Saturday 9am–6pm, Sunday by appointment.
activities.address: Rambaud Hill, Route de Marigot–Grand Case, 97150 Saint-Martin

activities.name: NO1SXM
activities.hook: Two hours on a racing trimaran as the sun goes down, fourteen people maximum.
activities.desc: Captain Pieter has forty-five years of charter behind him, in Europe and the Caribbean. The sunset sail is two hours with cocktails and snacks, $55 a head and $39 for children, maximum fourteen aboard; the day sail runs five hours. Meet at the Nowhere Special dock in Simpson Bay — 4:30pm in winter, 5pm in summer — and a dinghy takes you out to the boat.
activities.address: Meeting point: Nowhere Special, Welfare Rd 88, Simpson Bay

activities.name: Parotte Ville Bird Park
activities.hook: A half-hour with the parrots, hand-feeding included — George's quiet corner of Belvedere.
activities.desc: A small family-run aviary and medicinal garden in Belvedere. Guided tours run about thirty minutes and include feeding ring-neck parakeets, sun conures, brown-throated conures and black-headed caiques. There is a museum on site too.
activities.address: Bishop Hill Road, Belvedere, Philipsburg, Sint Maarten

activities.name: Patty Healing Hands
activities.hook: Twenty-four years on the island, and she comes to the villa.
activities.desc: Patty has been practicing on SXM for twenty-four years — hot stone, acupressure, reflexology, relaxation and Reiki, plus therapeutic work on injuries and pain. She travels anywhere on the island and will come to the villa. Book at least a week ahead; she fills up.
activities.address: Mobile — comes to the villa

activities.name: Pharmacie Bellevue
activities.hook: A full pharmacy on the edge of Marigot — and the place for French skincare.

activities.address: Zone d'Activité Bellevue, 97150 Marigot, Saint-Martin

activities.name: Pic Paradis
activities.hook: 424 m, the highest point on the island — both coasts from one spot.

activities.address: Route du Pic Paradis, Colombier, 97150 Saint-Martin

activities.name: Rainforest Adventures

activities.address: 59 L.B. Scott Road, Philipsburg, Sint Maarten

activities.name: Rotary Lookout Point

activities.address: Quartier d'Orléans, 97150 Saint-Martin

activities.name: Sail Renegades
activities.hook: All-inclusive catamaran days to Anguilla, St. Barts and around.
activities.desc: Private catamaran charters out of Port de Plaisance, with crew, food and drink included and custom itineraries across St. Martin, Anguilla and St. Barts. Sunset and lunch sails run year-round.

activities.name: Seaside Nature Park

activities.name: SXM One Island
activities.hook: Island caps and tees that don't look like airport souvenirs.

activities.name: The Art Box Gallery
activities.hook: Thirty-odd Caribbean artists under one roof, and things you can actually carry home.

activities.name: Super U Hope Estate
activities.hook: The big French supermarket at Hope Estate — everything under one roof.

## Oven — Brandt BXP6332B

Manual: Brandt *Guide d'utilisation – Four / User Guide – Oven*, code CZ5703038-00, 07-2016 (FR + EN; cover models BXP6330X, BXP5560B, **BXP6332X**, BXP6355X — the BXP6332X is this oven in stainless; the black BXP6332B shares the same programmer, keys and functions). Read via manualmachine.com/brandt/bxp6330x (Brandt's own site timed out on 23 Sep; the printed notice in the house will be this document). Verbatim page numbers from the identical Brandt BXC6332X notice, fc.darty.com/notices/DOCUMENTATION/2016/52/4250745_NOTCOMP.pdf. Pyrolysis wording from Brandt CZ5703033-00 (07-2016).
Where: kitchen, lower unit of the tall stack (the Neff microwave is above it). Circuit "Four" on the breaker panel by the front door.

**The controls** (p.10): a rotary **function selector** (0 · the cooking modes · Pyro) and four keys — **[1] clock / duration** (clock symbol), **[2] temperature**, **[3] –**, **[4] +**. Display shows the time, temperature, a preheat indicator, a bell for the minute-minder, a padlock for the keypad lock and a door-lock symbol.

**Q: The display is flashing 12:00.** That's the clock asking to be set after a power cut — it happens often here, and the generator changeover does it too. Press **+** or **–** to the right time, then press **[1]** to confirm (p.11 §3.1). The manual says the oven only cooks once the time shows steadily (p.12 §4.1); set it first and everything behaves. *(Jordy, 23 Sep 2026: the clock is rarely set here and he hasn't noticed the oven refusing to heat — to be checked; until then the concierge gives the "set it first" answer, which is harmless either way.)*

**Q: How do I just cook something?** Turn the **selector** to a mode. It starts straight away at a suggested temperature; the temperature indicator flashes while it preheats and a series of beeps tells you it's there (p.12 §4.1). To change the temperature: press **[2]**, set with **+ / –**, press **[2]** again (p.12 §4.2). To stop: turn the selector back to **0**.

**Q: Which setting for what?** (p.11) **CHALEUR TOURNANTE** (fan) 35–235 °C — most things: fish, vegetables, several trays at once. **TRADITIONNEL PULSÉ** — roasts and fish in a dish. **GRIL PULSÉ** 180–230 — roast chicken or a leg of lamb, juicy and crisp; put the drip tray on the bottom shelf. **SOLE PULSÉE** (bottom heat + fan) — quiches, fruit tarts, cakes, soufflés. **TRADITIONNEL** — slow, delicate dishes, red-meat roasts, casseroles. **GRIL FORT** 180–275 — toast and gratins, drip tray underneath. **ECO** — no preheat, gentle, for when you're not in a hurry. Pizza: the recipe table (p.17–18) says 200 °C, shelf 2, 30–40 min. Shelves are numbered 1 (bottom) to 6 (top).

**Q: Can I set it to stop by itself?** Yes. While it's cooking press **[1]** — the duration flashes (the oven proposes 30 min on most modes) — set with **+ / –**; it saves itself after a few seconds and counts down once the oven is hot (p.12 §4.3). At the end it beeps; turn the selector to **0**. To have it *finish* at a given time: set the duration, press **[1]** again, set the end time with **+ / –** (p.12 §4.4).

**Q: The minute-minder?** With the oven off, press **[1]**, set minutes with **+ / –**, press **[1]** to start. Any key silences the beep; set 00:00 to cancel (p.11 §3.3).

**Q: Nothing responds and there's a padlock on the display.** The keypad lock. Press **+ and – together** until the padlock disappears (p.11 §3.4). Same gesture locks it.

**Q: It heats but the display says "demo" / nothing gets hot.** There's a demonstration mode in the MENU. Please don't go into MENU — message us and we'll walk you through it (p.13 §6.1).

**Q: Can I turn the beeps or the light off?** Both live in the MENU (hold **[1]** until MENU shows). We'd rather you left the MENU alone — the light goes off by itself after 90 s anyway (p.13 §6.1).

**Q: The fan is still running after I switched it off.** Normal — the cooling fan runs up to an hour after use (p.14 §7).

**Q: The door won't open and there's a lock symbol.** The oven is in a pyrolysis (self-clean) cycle: 2 hours, door locked, very hot. Wait for the display to show 0:00 and the lock symbol to go, then turn the selector to 0 (§5.2). Please don't start one — see below.

**Lights and codes** (p.14 §7): flashing **12:00** = power cut, set the clock · flashing **door-lock symbol** = a door-lock fault, message us · oven not heating with the clock set = check the breaker panel by the front door, otherwise message us · light out = message us (special 300 °C bulb).

**Please don't:** turn the selector to **Pyro** — it locks the door for two hours at cleaning temperature; the oven is cleaned between stays · use the oven door as a step or a shelf · scrub the door glass with anything abrasive · remove the door glass (p.8–9, p.13).

**Safety:** the door glass and the front get hot; open the door slowly; cook with the door closed; keep small children away from the front (p.8).

**Message us instead:** the door-lock symbol flashing · smoke or a burning smell that isn't food · the oven dead with the clock set and no breaker tripped · a cooling fan still running after more than an hour.

## Microwave — Neff C17WR00N0

Manual: Neff *Microwave — Instruction manual*, models C17WR01N0. / C17WR00N0., BSH doc 9000967437 rev A, 20 May 2014, 24 pp, English — media3.bsh-group.com/Documents/9000967437_A.pdf (Neff/BSH's own server).
Where: kitchen, upper unit of the tall stack, above the oven. No turntable — food goes in the middle of the floor of the compartment (p.12, 18).

**The controls** (p.7): touch buttons **on/off**, **Main menu**, **Time-setting option** (timer), **i** (info), **Automatic door opening**, **Start/Stop**, and the **ShiftControl** arrows — **Left / Right** change a value, **Up / Down** move between lines.

**Q: How do I open it?** Press the **door-opening button**; the door springs open and you pull it the rest of the way (p.8). In a power cut the button doesn't work — pull the door by hand.

**Q: Heat something up, simply.** Press **on/off** — 900 W comes up as the suggestion. **Left/Right** to pick a lower power if you want one, **Down**, **Left/Right** to set the time, **Start/Stop** (p.10). Mid-cook, **Left/Right** changes the time; **Up** then **Left/Right** changes the power (p.11). Opening the door pauses it; after closing it you must press **Start/Stop** again — it won't resume by itself (p.8–9).

**Q: Which power?** (p.10) **900 W** drinks and liquids (max 30 min) · **600 W** heating and cooking food, ready meals, soups · **360 W** cooking meat, warming delicate food, a baby bottle · **180 W** defrosting, butter · **90 W** gentle defrosting.

**Q: Defrost by weight?** **on/off** → **Main menu** → Left/Right to **Programmes** → Down → pick Defrost Bread / Meat / Fish (or Cook: fresh or frozen vegetables, potatoes, rice) → Down → set the weight → **Start/Stop**. It tells you when to turn or stir: open, do it, close, press **Start/Stop** again (p.12–13).

**Q: It's beeping at me.** That's "done". Press the **timer** button to stop it early (p.11).

**Q: It's asking me for a language and a time.** After a power cut (the generator changeover counts) it wants Language, Time and Date: use Down/Left/Right/Up, **Right** to confirm each (p.8). Two minutes and you're back.

**Q: It runs but nothing gets hot.** If a "demo" symbol is showing it's in demonstration mode — message us; the fix needs the power cut and a setting changed within three minutes (p.14, 16). Otherwise: is the door fully closed? (p.16)

**Q: A timer without cooking?** Press the **timer** button, set up to 24 h with Left/Right; it runs with the microwave off; set to zero to cancel (p.11).

**Lights and codes** (p.16): won't start = door not fully closed · **E0532** = open and close the door · **E6501** = switch off, wait 10 min, switch on · any other **Exxx** = switch off and on; if it comes back, message us with the code · blank display = check the breaker panel by the front door · light out = message us.

**Please don't** (p.4–6): run it empty · use metal, foil or gold/silver-rimmed dishes · heat sealed jars, packets, eggs in their shell or shellfish · heat oil on its own · dry clothes or warm grain pillows in it. Prick skins (potatoes, sausages). Put a spoon in a cup of liquid so it can't boil over suddenly. Stir baby food and test it. Anyone with a pacemaker or insulin pump: keep 10 cm from the front — there are magnets in the panel.

**Safety:** dishes come out hot — use a cloth; steam escapes when the door opens (p.6).

**Message us instead:** an E-code that comes back after switching off and on · the demo symbol · sparks · the door not latching.

## Kitchen fridge — Samsung RFG23UERS

Manual: Samsung *Refrigerator user manual — Free Standing Appliance*, DA99-03403F (EN)-14, 10 Jul 2019, 32 pp, model family RFG23U* — Samsung UK support page for RFG23UERS1/XEU, "User Manual, English, ver. 14" (org.downloadcenter.samsung.com …/DA99-03403F_EN-14_190710.pdf).
Where: kitchen. Water and ice come from the dispenser in the left door; the water is filtered (and the house water is already filtered and UV-treated before it gets here — safe to drink, see island-facts §6).

**The panel** (p.20): left — **Energy Saver** · **Freezer / Power Freeze (3 sec)** · **Alarm / Reset Filter (3 sec)**; right — **Lighting** · **Fridge / Power Cool (3 sec)** · **Ice Off / Child Lock (3 sec)**; below the display **Ice** and **Water**. Indicators: Filter, Cubed, Crushed, Water, Ice Off, Child Lock.

**Q: Water?** Press **Water**, push the glass gently against the lever, wait a second before pulling away (p.21). If it's been unused a couple of days, pour the first glass or two away (p.22). Cloudy water is just air bubbles — it clears in seconds.

**Q: Ice?** Press **Ice** — each press switches Cubed ↔ Crushed — then push the lever with the glass (p.21). Pressing Ice cancels Water and vice versa. If the door is open the dispenser won't run (p.21).

**Q: No ice comes out.** Check **Ice Off** isn't lit on the display (press it to toggle, p.21). After a reset or an empty bucket it needs about 8 hours to make the first cubes, and up to 24 h to fill (p.22). Still nothing? Message us — please don't press the test button inside the ice maker.

**Q: The ice has clumped / the bucket is stuck.** Pull the **lock lever** forward, take the bucket out, break the clump, push the bucket back until it clicks (p.22). Dry cloth only, never wash the bucket.

**Q: The panel does nothing when I press it.** Child Lock: hold **Ice Off / Child Lock** for 3 seconds — that locks the display and dispenser; hold the same button 3 s again to release (p.20 gives the lock step; the release is the same button). Also, some buttons act after a short delay; that's normal (p.20).

**Q: It's beeping.** The door-open alarm. Close the doors properly; press **Alarm** to silence it (p.20).

**Q: The TV switched itself off / the art disappeared.** Art Mode goes dark when nobody's moved in the room for a while, and at night when the room is dark (**Night Mode**) — both by design (e-manual p.52–60; Samsung TSG10002347). Walk past it or press Power.

**Q: HDMI for my laptop/console?** The ports are on the One Connect Box in the cabinet — message us rather than opening it.

## Air conditioning — Daikin (bedrooms FTX35K, living room FTX50K)

Manual: Daikin *Room Air Conditioner Operation Manual*, FTX20/25/35/50/60/71K2V1B, doc 3P393186-3W (2016.12), and FTX50/60/71KMV1B, doc 3P393186-8E (2015.07) — both on daikin.eu's document library; the two are word-for-word identical. Page refs are to 3W. The remote the manual illustrates has direct mode buttons (AUTO/OFF/COOL/DRY/HEAT/FAN ONLY); Daikin doesn't print its part number.
Where: one wall unit and one remote per room — living room, master bedroom, downstairs bedroom, upstairs bedroom (the fifth is in the owners' closet). The remote is mounted on the wall, usually near the door and next to the fan remote (Jordy, 23 Sep 2026). Caribbean-style, please switch it off when you go out or turn in (rooms cool back down in minutes).

**The remote** (p.8): **COOL · DRY · HEAT · FAN ONLY · AUTO** start that mode at once; **OFF** stops; **TEMP ▲/▼**; **FAN**; **SWING**; **COMFORT**; **POWERFUL**; **ECONO**; in the TIMER box **ON**, **OFF** and **CANCEL**. The unit beeps twice on start, once on a change, and gives a long beep on stop (p.5).

**Q: Cool the room.** Press **COOL**, then **TEMP ▼/▲** to 24–26 °C — Daikin suggests 26–28 (p.10–11). Range 18–32 °C. Press **OFF** to stop.

**Q: It's showing °F / I want °F.** Hold **TEMP ▲** and the timer **ON** button together about 5 s while a temperature is showing — it switches °C ↔ °F (p.9).

**Q: Fan speed?** **FAN** cycles AUTO → quiet → 1 to 5 (p.12). Lower is quieter and cools a little less.

**Q: The air blows on the bed.** Press **COMFORT** — the flap lifts so air doesn't blow on people (p.14). Or **SWING** to sweep, and **SWING** again to lock the flap where you like it (p.13). Don't move the flap by hand; the side louvres inside the outlet are the only ones you move with your fingers.

**Q: Turn off after two hours?** Press **OFF** in the TIMER box — each press adds an hour, up to 12; the orange TIMER lamp lights (p.16). **CANCEL** clears it. With an OFF timer set the unit eases the setpoint up half a degree so you don't wake cold (Night Set, p.16). Timers are lost after a power cut.

**Q: Cool it down fast.** **POWERFUL** — full blast for 20 minutes, then it drops back by itself (p.14). **ECONO** does the opposite — caps the power (p.15).

**Q: What's DRY?** Dehumidify; it picks its own temperature and fan — you can't set them in DRY (p.10). COOL at 25–26 with a low fan is the better everyday setting.

**Q: The temperature won't change / FAN does nothing.** You're in DRY or POWERFUL (p.10, 14). Press **COOL**.

**Q: It won't start.** Check the remote batteries (2 × AAA, slide the back cover down, p.9), that you're within ~7 m with nothing in the way, and that the room's breaker isn't tripped (panel by the front door). If it just stopped, it may be a 3-minute protection pause — wait (p.27). After a power cut it restarts itself in about 3 minutes (p.28).

**Q: The green light is blinking.** A fault. Switch it **OFF**, wait, press **COOL** again. Still blinking: hold **CANCEL** about 5 s until "00" flashes on the remote, tap **CANCEL** until you hear one long beep, and message us the two characters showing (p.31).

**Q: Mist from the unit / dripping outside / gurgles and clicks.** All normal (p.28–29). Water dripping *inside* the room is not — message us.

**Q: It's not cold enough.** Windows and doors closed? Fan on quiet or 1? ECONO on? Something in front of the unit? (p.29–30). Above 32 °C indoors or very humid it may drip — close up the room first.

**Please don't:** hang anything on the unit or put a vase on it · poke fingers or objects into the inlet or outlet · use spray cans near it · run it with windows open · leave it on when you go out for the day (p.3–4; house rule).

**Message us instead:** the OPERATION lamp blinking after a restart · water inside · a burning smell (switch it off first) · a breaker that trips again.

Easiest: the panel by the front door → **Rooms** — on/off, speed 1–5, light. **Remotes** are labelled and wall-mounted in their rooms, usually near the door next to the AC remote (Jordy, 23 Sep 2026). Three exceptions: the **upper patio** has two remotes, both kept in the **master bedroom** — one for the fan by the master, one paired remote that drives the front and middle patio fans together; the **lower patio**'s front and middle fans share one paired remote that lives **just inside the front door**. **Q: Which remote is the patio?** Upstairs: both are in the master bedroom — "master" runs the fan outside that room, the other runs the two along the patio together. Downstairs: the remote just inside the front door runs both lower-patio fans at once. Or use the panel → Rooms → Exterior.

**The remote** (§15, p.27–28): **FAN** on/off (starts at speed 3) · fan **+ / –** speed 1–5 · **LIGHT** on/off · light **+ / –** brightness · **CCT** warm/neutral/cool white · **TIMER** each press +1 h, up to 12 · **MODE** short press NORMAL → SLEEP → ECO; **hold MODE ~3 s** = reverse.

**Q: The speed buttons stopped working.** You're in SLEEP or ECO (§15): press **MODE** until the screen shows NORMAL.

**Q: Light too bright / too white.** Light **–** to dim; **CCT** to change the colour of the white (§15).

- One island, two countries, since the Treaty of Concordia of 23 March 1648. ## 17. Health and safety

- Tap water: see §6 — officially potable on the French side; the villa filters it further. — checked 22 Sep 2026
- Mosquitoes: dengue, chikungunya and Zika are all present in the region; Santé publique France's Antilles bulletins of 2 Apr and 22 May 2026 rate the dengue situation in Saint-Martin as calm. Use an EPA/EU-registered repellent (DEET, picaridin, PMD), light long clothing at dusk, and keep screens/AC on; keep protecting for three weeks after travel. — source: https://www.santepubliquefrance.fr/regions-et-territoires/antilles/bulletin-regional/dengue-aux-antilles-bulletin-du-22-mai-2026; https://travel.gc.ca/destinations/sint-maarten; https://www.cdc.gov/mosquitoes/prevention/preventing-mosquito-bites-while-traveling.html (21 Nov 2024), checked 22 Sep 2026
- Sargassum: Orient Bay faces east, the direction the rafts arrive from, so it is among the first beaches to get seaweed. Season roughly April–September, heaviest May–August, clearest December–March; year to year varies (2025 set records). Météo-France posts a 4-day stranding forecast for Saint-Martin ("Îles du Nord") at https://meteofrance.gp/fr/sargasses/iles-du-nord; on 21 Sep 2026 it showed scattered arrivals on the east/south-east coasts, improving. The Collectivité installs deflection barriers in Cul-de-Sac bay (Aug 2026) and at the Embouchure (Oct 2026). Beaches that rarely get it: Grand Case, Anse Marcel, Friar's/Happy Bay, Baie Rouge, Baie Longue, Simpson Bay, Mullet, Cupecoy, Maho, Great Bay, Little Bay. — source: https://meteofrance.gp/fr/sargasses/iles-du-nord (21 Sep 2026); https://meteofrance.mq/fr/sargasses/comprendre-la-proliferation-massive-des-sargasses-en-2025-dynamiques-climatiques (21 Jul 2025); https://outremers360.com/bassin-atlantique-appli/saint-martin-des-barrages-deviants-anti-sargasses-installes-des-aout (1 Aug 2026); https://sealaviesxm.com/sargassum-st-maarten (21 Sep 2026); https://bookstmartin.com/sargassum-st-martin/ (6 Jul 2026), checked 22 Sep 2026
- Rotting sargassum releases hydrogen sulphide (rotten-egg smell): avoid stretches with fresh or rotting weed and the collection heaps; anyone with asthma or a heart condition, pregnant women and small children should be careful; see a doctor if eyes/throat irritation or headache persist. — source: https://www.guadeloupe.ars.sante.fr/informations-sargasses (3 Nov 2022), checked 22 Sep 2026
- Sea conditions: Orient Bay gets onshore trade-wind chop, calmest in the morning; the northern end and the Atlantic-facing beaches (Guana Bay, Dawn Beach outside the reef) have real currents and rips. Guana Bay is for strong swimmers only. Le Galion (10 min away) is reef-protected and flat — the one for small children. There are no lifeguards on the island's beaches. — source: https://www.visitstmaarten.com/safety/ (7 Apr 2026); https://www.vacationstmaarten.com/listing/guana-bay-beach/261/; https://www.visitstmaarten.com/beaches/le-galion/ (19 Mar 2026); https://travel.gc.ca/destinations/sint-maarten; guide records B1, B2, B14 (content export), checked 22 Sep 2026
- Sea urchins: on rocks and at Moses Walk / Caye Chateau; wear water shoes. If spined: remove visible spines promptly, soak in vinegar, hot-water immersion for pain; deeply embedded spines or a spine near a joint need a doctor. — source: https://www.merckmanuals.com/home/injuries-and-poisoning/bites-and-stings/sea-urchin-stings; guide record A23, checked 22 Sep 2026
- Maho Beach jet blast: departing jets have killed (a tourist in July 2017) and seriously injured people holding the fence; official signs warn of death or serious injury. Watch landings; stand well back and never hold the fence during take-offs. — source: https://nltimes.nl/2017/07/13/woman-killed-jet-blast-sint-maarten-airport; https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Maho_Beach, checked 22 Sep 2026
- Sun: tropical UV year-round (typical daily max index ~7); the trade wind hides the heat. Hat, SPF, shade at midday. — source: UV figure from weather-atlas.com only (not corroborated) — treat as approximate; see Unresolved.
- French-side hospital: Centre Hospitalier Louis-Constant Fleming, Concordia, Marigot (≈25 min from the villa off-peak). ER +590 590 52 26 29 (24 h, all ages); switchboard +590 590 52 25 25. For a life-threatening emergency call 15 — the SAMU dispatches and decides the transport. — source: https://www.sante.fr/centre-hospitalier-ch/saint-martin/centre-hospitalier-louis-constant-fleming/urgences-generales (updated 29 Jun 2026); https://www.st-martin.org/us/organizing-your-stay/useful-informations/, checked 22 Sep 2026

Rarely above 34 °C or below 20 °C. — source: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Saint_Martin_(island), checked 22 Sep 2026
